# Frontend Build Plan — "The University"

The learner-facing web interface for Open CS Degree 2026.

**Decisions (locked 2026-07-18):** static site generated by **Astro** from the
curriculum data, served by **Caddy**; learner progress in a **git-backed file**
(working copy in browser localStorage); **local-first** hosting with a
copy-paste promotion path to a VPS.

## Architecture

```
curriculum/pathway.yaml ─┐
resources/registry.yaml ─┼─► Astro build (site/) ─► site/dist/ ─► Caddy ─► browser
curriculum/**/*.md ──────┘         ▲                                  │
      (OKF documents)              └── Zod schemas mirror the OKF     │
                                       profile (planning/01)          ▼
                                                     localStorage (working copy)
                                                          ⇅ import/export
                                              learner-state repo/branch: progress.yaml
                                                          ⇅ reconcile script
                                                   /teach learning record
```

Principles:

- **The site is a pure function of the repo.** Every `git push` that touches
  curriculum data can rebuild it; nothing on the server is mutable state.
- **Curriculum is shared, progress is personal** (charter): learner state never
  enters this repo. The site *reads* progress from the browser and syncs it to
  a private git location the learner owns.
- **`/teach` delivers lessons; the site delivers orientation.** The site is the
  campus — catalog, map, dashboard, library. Lesson delivery stays in `/teach`.

## Repository layout

```
site/                      # Astro project (this repo — monorepo)
  astro.config.mjs
  src/
    content.config.ts      # Zod schemas mirroring the OKF profile
    loaders/               # readers for pathway.yaml + registry.yaml
    pages/
      index.astro          # dashboard
      pathway.astro        # interactive prerequisite map
      courses/[id].astro   # course pages
      courses/[id]/[...concept].astro   # concept pages (Phase 3 content)
      library.astro        # source registry + license status
      tracks/[track].astro
    components/            # CourseCard, KaBadge, LicenseBadge, ProgressRing…
    islands/               # the few interactive bits (see below)
  public/
Caddyfile                  # local block now, commented VPS block for later
```

## Pages

| Route | Content | Data source |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | Dashboard: current courses, **next available courses** (DAG frontier given completed set), overall credit progress, per-KA progress | pathway.yaml + progress |
| `/pathway` | Full prerequisite map, semester-grouped, color-coded by track; completed/available/locked states overlaid | pathway.yaml + progress |
| `/courses/CS2201` | Course page: description, prerequisites (with met/unmet status), units, reading list with license badges, project, **"Study this in /teach"** panel rendering the mission | course bundle + registry |
| `/courses/CS2201/…` | Concept pages rendered from OKF documents as Phase 3 fills them in | curriculum markdown |
| `/library` | Every registry source with status badge (`open`/`purchased`/`approval_requested`…), filterable; doubles as your licensing dashboard | registry.yaml |
| `/tracks/ai` | Track overview and its five courses | pathway.yaml |

## Interactive islands (client-side JS only where earned)

1. **Pathway map** — render the DAG client-side (Cytoscape.js or d3-dag;
   decide in FE-1 by prototyping both with the real 45-node graph). Nodes get
   three visual states from progress: completed / available (all prereqs met) /
   locked. Clicking a node → course page.
2. **Progress tracker** — mark a course or concept complete; recompute the
   frontier instantly. State lives in localStorage under a versioned key.
3. **Search** — Pagefind at build time; static, no server, scales to the full
   Phase 3 corpus.

Everything else is zero-JS static HTML.

## Progress: git-backed with a localStorage working copy

A static site cannot write to disk, so the flow is:

1. **Working copy:** every checkbox/quiz interaction updates
   `localStorage.openCS.progress` immediately — the site always feels live.
2. **Sync out:** dashboard "Export progress" downloads `progress.yaml`
   (schema below). The learner keeps it in a private repo or branch
   (`learner-state`), committed like any file. A helper `scripts/progress_sync.py`
   (FE-2) automates: pull → merge with an exported file → commit → push.
3. **Sync in:** "Import progress" loads `progress.yaml` from disk — this is
   also the cross-device story (push on the desktop, import on the laptop).
4. **`/teach` reconciliation:** the same helper can read `/teach`'s learning
   record and mark matching concepts complete in `progress.yaml`, so lessons
   taken in `/teach` show up on the dashboard.

```yaml
# progress.yaml (lives in the learner's private repo — never in this one)
learner: anesu
updated: 2026-07-18
completed_courses: [CS1101, MA1101]
in_progress: [CS1102]
completed_concepts:
  - cs1102.gates.boolean-logic
quiz_scores: {}          # populated by /teach reconciliation
```

Merge rule for conflicts: union of completed sets, newest quiz score wins —
progress only ever grows, which makes git merges trivial.

## Caddy

`Caddyfile` at repo root:

```caddyfile
# ── local (now) ────────────────────────────────
localhost:8080 {
    root * site/dist
    file_server
    encode zstd gzip
    handle_errors {
        rewrite * /404.html
        file_server
    }
}

# ── VPS promotion (later): replace the site block's address ──
# university.example.com {
#     root * /srv/opencs/dist
#     file_server
#     encode zstd gzip
# }   # Caddy provisions HTTPS automatically once DNS points here
```

Promotion to a VPS is: copy `dist/` (rsync or a git pull + build on the box),
swap the address line, done. No config rewrite, no TLS work.

## Build & CI

- Local: `cd site && npm run dev` (hot reload) or `npm run build` + `caddy run`.
- CI: extend `.github/workflows/validate.yml` with a `site-build` job — the
  Astro build **fails on schema violations** (Zod mirrors the OKF profile), so
  bad frontmatter breaks CI twice: once in the Python validator, once in the
  site build. Build artifact uploaded; deployment stays manual until the VPS
  exists.

## Phasing

| Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| **FE-1 Skeleton** | Astro scaffold; loaders for pathway + registry; course pages, track pages, library, static pathway map (Mermaid image to start); Caddyfile; CI build job | Site builds from real data and serves at `localhost:8080` |
| **FE-2 Progress** | localStorage progress island; dashboard with DAG frontier ("what can I study next"); export/import; `progress_sync.py` | Mark CS1101 complete → CS1201/CS1202/CS1203 unlock on the map |
| **FE-3 Interactive map** | Cytoscape/d3 pathway island with completed/available/locked states replacing the static map | Full 45-node graph usable on desktop + phone |
| **FE-4 Content & search** | Concept-page rendering for OKF documents; Pagefind search; `/teach` mission panel on course pages | One full course (pilot from Phase 2/3) readable end-to-end |
| **FE-5 VPS promotion** | Domain + VPS, deploy script, HTTPS via Caddy | Site reachable from your phone |

FE-1 needs nothing beyond the data that already exists. FE-4 depends on
curriculum Phases 2–3 producing course bundles and concept documents.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- No accounts, no auth, no server-side state — revisit only if this becomes
  multi-learner (that's the "Static + small API" fork we deliberately skipped).
- No lesson player — `/teach` owns lesson delivery.
- No CMS — content is edited in git, that's the point.
